title: Functions and Function Notation
goals: What makes a relation a function; reading and evaluating f(x).
why: Joined with 1.5 in the day 1 hook and review; function notation is Algebra I work retrieved, not retaught.

title: Domain and Range
goals: Domain and range from graphs, rules and situations, in interval notation; piecewise rules.
why: The review day that adds interval notation, the unit's one new tool.

title: Rates of Change and Behavior of Graphs
goals: Average rate of change; where a graph rises and falls; relative extrema.
why: Rising, falling and extrema on day 3; the average rate of change on day 149, where pc-rates-of-change uses it.
order_conflict: The average rate of change moves from chapter 1 to unit 10.
harms_learning: no: unit 1 needs only the graph behavior, and the rate is taught where secant slopes build on it (filed under unit 1; day 149 is unit 10)

title: Composition of Functions
goals: Composite functions from formulas, tables and graphs; their domains; splitting a function into parts.
why: Four days, by the load of pc-composition.

title: Transformation of Functions
goals: Shifts, stretches and reflections; even and odd functions.
why: Retrieved on day 1; even and odd tested algebraically on day 4.

title: Absolute Value Functions
goals: Absolute value graphs and equations.
why: Read as a piecewise rule beside symmetry on day 4; absolute value equations are Algebra I work and are not retaught.

title: Inverse Functions
goals: Inverses checked by composition, read from graphs and tables, made by restricting a domain.
why: One day per lettered part.

title: Linear Functions
goals: Linear rules, slope and intercept.
why: Algebra I owns linear functions; no day only reteaches it.

title: Graphs of Linear Functions
goals: Graphing lines; parallel and perpendicular lines.
why: Algebra I and Geometry own it; the perpendicular slopes return inside day 135.

title: Modeling with Linear Functions
goals: Linear models of situations.
why: Algebra I owns linear modeling.

title: Fitting Linear Models to Data
goals: Lines of fit and correlation.
why: Algebra I fits lines and Statistics owns regression; day 41 fits a line to straightened data inside its own task.

title: Complex Numbers
goals: Complex arithmetic; division by the conjugate.
why: The review day of complex arithmetic, with division by the conjugate as the new part.

title: Quadratic Functions
goals: Quadratic forms and graphs.
why: Algebra I and Algebra II own quadratics.

title: Power Functions and Polynomial Functions
goals: Degree, leading term and end behavior.
why: End behavior retrieved on the day 18 review with 3.4 and 3.5.

title: Graphs of Polynomial Functions
goals: Zeros, multiplicity and turning points on a graph.
why: Retrieval of Algebra II zeros and multiplicity on day 18.

title: Dividing Polynomials
goals: Long and synthetic division; the Remainder Theorem.
why: Retrieval of the Remainder Theorem, with synthetic division added as a shortcut.

title: Zeros of Polynomial Functions
goals: Rational candidates, the factor theorem, the fundamental theorem of algebra and conjugate pairs.
why: Five days, by the load of pc-polynomial-complex-zeros.

title: Rational Functions
goals: Asymptotes, holes and graphs of rational functions.
why: A review day of Algebra II graphs, then slant asymptotes and sign on each interval.
order_conflict: Taught after our rational-expression days (24 to 26).
harms_learning: no: the expression work comes first because reading a function from its factored form uses it

title: Inverses and Radical Functions
goals: Inverses of polynomial functions with restricted domains; radical functions.
why: Joined to 1.7 for domain restriction.
harms_learning: no: it needs only inverses, and units 3 and 4 need the restriction early

title: Modeling Using Variation
goals: Direct, inverse and joint variation.
why: Grade 7 and Algebra I proportional reasoning; no pc- row owns it.

title: Exponential Functions
goals: Exponential rules from points; continuous growth with e.
why: Retrieved on the day 33 review with 4.2 and 4.3.

title: Graphs of Exponential Functions
goals: Exponential graphs and their transformations.
why: Retrieved as the graph a logarithm reflects.

title: Logarithmic Functions
goals: The logarithm as the inverse of the exponential; common and natural logarithms.
why: Two days: the inverse idea, then checking by composition.

title: Graphs of Logarithmic Functions
goals: Logarithmic graphs as reflections in y = x.
why: With 4.3 on day 34.

title: Logarithmic Properties
goals: Product, quotient and power properties; change of base.
why: The properties, then the change of base.

title: Exponential and Logarithmic Equations
goals: Exact solutions; rejecting inputs outside the domain.

title: Exponential and Logarithmic Models
goals: Half-life, doubling, logarithmic scales and logistic growth.
why: Half-life, scales and the logistic model on three days; our own data sets.
harms_learning: no: straightening data first gives the paper route the logistic fit uses

title: Fitting Exponential Models to Data
goals: Exponential, logarithmic and logistic fits with technology.
why: Plus straightening on semi-log paper (ours).

title: Angles
goals: Radians, arc length and angles in standard position.
why: Retrieval of radians on the day 50 review.

title: Unit Circle: Sine and Cosine Functions
goals: Special angles and reference angles on the unit circle.
why: Special triangles, then reference angles.

title: The Other Trigonometric Functions
goals: Reciprocal functions; even and odd; periodicity.
why: Symmetry and periodicity on day 52; the six values on day 54.

title: Right Triangle Trigonometry
goals: Ratios in right triangles.
why: Retrieval of Geometry's ratios for the special triangles.
harms_learning: no: the special triangles are where the exact values come from

title: Graphs of the Sine and Cosine Functions
goals: Amplitude, period, phase shift and midline.
why: The two review days of Algebra II graphs, phase shift added.

title: Graphs of the Other Trigonometric Functions
goals: Tangent, cotangent, secant and cosecant graphs.
why: Tangent and cotangent, then secant and cosecant.

title: Inverse Trigonometric Functions
goals: Restricted domains; evaluating inverse functions.
why: Restriction, then evaluation.

title: Solving Trigonometric Equations with Identities
goals: Verifying identities; simplifying with them.
why: Proof chains on days 66 and 72; equations that need an identity on day 74.

title: Sum and Difference Identities
goals: Addition and subtraction formulas and exact values.
why: Cosine first, then sine and tangent.

title: Double-Angle, Half-Angle, and Reduction Formulas
goals: Double-angle, power-reducing and half-angle formulas.
why: The power-reducing formulas taught as the step to the half-angle formulas.

title: Sum-to-Product and Product-to-Sum Formulas
goals: Converting sums and products.
why: Not owned by any row; the product-to-sum derivation stays as an optional extension inside day 72.

title: Solving Trigonometric Equations
goals: Exact and technology solutions; solutions in an interval and in general.
why: Special angles, then factoring or identities, then technology.

title: Modeling with Trigonometric Equations
goals: Periodic models solved for a time.
why: Solving with an inverse function in unit 4; equations needing an identity in unit 5.
order_conflict: Its first part (day 62) comes before 7.1 to 7.5.
harms_learning: no: F-TF.B.7 needs only the inverse functions of unit 4 (filed under unit 4; day 77 is unit 5)

title: Non-right Triangles: Law of Sines
goals: The area formula, the law of sines and the ambiguous case.
why: Area, law of sines, ambiguous case, then the surveying day.

title: Non-right Triangles: Law of Cosines
goals: The law of cosines.
why: Proof and use, then the surveying day; Heron's formula as an optional extension.

title: Polar Coordinates
goals: Plotting and converting polar coordinates.
why: Plotting, then converting.
harms_learning: no: the vector-arrow model comes before the complex plane, and rotation by a matrix before rotation by a complex number

title: Polar Coordinates: Graphs
goals: Polar graphs from tables and symmetry.
why: Circles and lines, limacons, roses and spirals, then matching.

title: Polar Form of Complex Numbers
goals: The complex plane, polar form, products and powers.
why: Powers kept, roots an optional extension; distance and midpoint (N-CN.B.6) added as ours on day 125.

title: Parametric Equations
goals: Parametric equations and eliminating the parameter.
why: Tables of t, then eliminating the parameter.

title: Parametric Equations: Graphs
goals: Graphing parametric curves; projectile paths.
why: Graphs, then the thrown-ball task.

title: Vectors
goals: Vectors, components, sums, scalar multiples, the dot product.
standards: N-VM.A.1; N-VM.A.2; N-VM.A.3; N-VM.B.4; N-VM.B.5; CUR-PC.9
why: Eight days, by the load of the two vector rows; the projection is ours (day 95).

goals: Three-variable systems.

goals: Nonlinear systems and inequalities.
why: Geometry owns A-REI.C.7 and Algebra I the graphing of inequalities; no pc- row owns it.

title: Partial Fractions
goals: Decomposing rational expressions.
why: Calculus teaches partial fractions where it uses them.

title: Matrices and Matrix Operations
goals: Matrix arithmetic and products.
why: Data in matrices, products, properties.

title: Solving Systems with Gaussian Elimination
goals: Row reduction.

title: Solving Systems with Inverses
goals: Inverse matrices and matrix equations.
why: The 2 by 2 inverse on day 105; solving with it on day 111.

title: Solving Systems with Cramer's Rule
goals: Determinants and Cramer's rule.
why: Not owned; the determinant is used for invertibility and area instead.

title: The Ellipse
goals: Ellipses from their foci; standard form.

title: The Hyperbola
goals: Hyperbolas from their foci; standard form and asymptotes.

why: Retrieval before infinite series.
